annotation.title_clean: Trading Robot Sales as Investment Fraud Under Indonesian Law
annotation.title_en: Trading Robot Sales as Investment Fraud Under Indonesian Law
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Pradana, F.E.; Arifin, Z.; Manfaluthi, A.
named_instruments_referenced: Indonesia Law No. 8 of 2010 on Money Laundering
Indonesia Law No. 7 of 2014 on Trade
annotation.summary_en: Normative legal study of Indonesian Supreme Court Decision 5522 K/Pid.Sus/2024 on trading robot sales as investment fraud, finding it met Criminal Code Article 378 fraud elements and was linked to money laundering. It calls for adaptive reform, stronger supervision and financial literacy. The 'robots' are software trading systems, not physical robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Trading robot scheme functioned as structured investment fraud, satisfying Article 378 KUHP.
Practice linked to money laundering under Law No. 8 of 2010.
Court used a substantive approach but consumer protection reasoning needs stronger integration.
Regulatory gaps, weak oversight and low financial literacy enable recurrence.
Recommends specific digital investment regulation and early warning mechanisms.
